library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pais_2026_cefepime_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Pais_2026_cefepime_rat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01005-25>

Pais 2026 gave intravenous cefepime to male Sprague-Dawley rats with
folic-acid-induced acute kidney injury (AKI), which prolongs the cefepime
plasma half-life about 10-fold, and scored seizures on a modified Racine scale.
Plasma was sampled after each daily dose and the cerebral cortex and
hippocampus were harvested once, at euthanasia. A three-compartment PK model
(plasma exchanging with cortex and with hippocampus) was fitted in Monolix, and
each rat's first-24-h exposures were then related to whether it reached a
convulsive seizure (stage > 1) by five separate logistic regressions
(Figure 5). The paper contributes six model files:

| Model | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_rat` | Three-compartment PK (plasma, cortex, hippocampus) |
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_aucplasma_rat` | P(stage > 1) vs plasma AUC0-24 (Figure 5a) |
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_auccortex_rat` | P(stage > 1) vs cortex AUC0-24 (Figure 5c) |
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_cmaxcortex_rat` | P(stage > 1) vs cortex Cmax0-24 (Figure 5d) |
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_auchippocampus_rat` | P(stage > 1) vs hippocampus AUC0-24 (Figure 5e) |
| `Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_cmaxhippocampus_rat` | P(stage > 1) vs hippocampus Cmax0-24 (Figure 5f) |

# Population

Eighteen male Sprague-Dawley rats, about 9-10 weeks old, mean (SD) weight
282 (17.0) g (Methods, 'Experimental design and animals'). AKI was induced with
folic acid 250 mg/kg intraperitoneally on day 1, followed in the multiple-dose
arm by 100 mg/kg daily. Cefepime was given intravenously 30 min after folic
acid, either 1,593 mg/kg once (serial sacrifice at 30 or 120 min on day 1) or
1,250 mg/kg once daily for up to 5 days (sacrifice at 120 min on day 3 or 5).
Plasma was sampled at 0, 15, 30 and 120 min after dosing; 127 of 129 plasma
concentrations and all 18 cortex and 18 hippocampus concentrations were
modelled (Results). Brain concentrations are total tissue concentrations in
ug/g, treated as mg/L by the model.

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: central <-> cortex, central <-> hippocampus, kel from central | -- | Figure 3 schematic; Methods 'Ordinary differential equations' (with the two corrections below) |
| `lkel` | 0.14 1/h | Table 2 (RSE 38.7%) |
| `lvc` | 0.12 L | Table 2 (RSE 6.85%) |
| `lv_brain_cortex` | 0.0039 L | Table 2 (RSE 18.6%) |
| `lv_brain_hippocampus` | 0.00039 L | Table 2 (RSE 14.8%) |
| `lk_central_brain_cortex` (k12) | 0.00013 1/h, fixed | Table 2 (no RSE); Discussion 'was fixed to reduce RSE%'; Table 1 selected model 'fixed k12' |
| `lk_brain_cortex_central` (k21) | 0.17 1/h | Table 2 (RSE 18.5%) |
| `lk_central_brain_hippocampus` (k13) | 0.000015 1/h | Table 2 (RSE 24.9%) |
| `lk_brain_hippocampus_central` (k31) | 0.15 1/h | Table 2 (RSE 31.2%) |
| `e_wt_kel` | 0.75, fixed | Table 2 'beta_kel_logtWT' (no RSE) |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Table 2 'beta_Vcentral_logtWT' (no RSE) |
| Weight reference | 0.282 kg | Methods (cohort mean 282 g); see Assumptions |
| IIV | not encoded | Table 2 prints only corr(kel, Vhippocampus) = 0.92 |
| Residual error | `fixed(0)` | not reported |
| TC50, plasma AUC0-24 | 30,658.6 mg*h/L | Results; Figure 5 legend |
| TC50, cortex AUC0-24 | 760.8 mg*h/L | Results; Figure 5 legend |
| TC50, cortex Cmax0-24 | 45.0 mg/L | Results; Figure 5 legend |
| TC50, hippocampus AUC0-24 | 838.2 mg*h/L | Results; Figure 5 legend |
| TC50, hippocampus Cmax0-24 | 48.2 mg/L | Results; Figure 5 legend |
| Logistic slopes (five) | 1.96e-4, 3.33e-3, 0.0590, 5.83e-3, 0.123 | digitised from Figure 5a, c, d, e, f |

## The printed equations

The Methods print the cortex equation as
`ddt_Acortex = k12*Acentral - (Acortex*k12)` and the cortex output as
`Ccortex = Acentral/Vcortex`. Read literally, k21 (estimated with an RSE of
18.5%) would appear nowhere, and the cortex concentration would be plasma
amount over a 4 mL volume, about `0.12 / 0.0039` = 31 times the plasma
concentration. The Results contradict that: the median cortex AUC0-24 is 565
against a plasma AUC0-24 of 28,314 mg*h/L, a ratio of 0.020. The Figure 3
schematic (k12 out, k21 back) gives a steady-state cortex:plasma ratio of
`k12 * Vc / (k21 * Vcortex)`, computed below; the hippocampus equations are
printed consistently with the schematic. The model therefore uses the
schematic.

```{r printed-equation-check}
p <- c(kel = 0.14, vc = 0.12, vcx = 0.0039, vhc = 0.00039,
       k12 = 0.00013, k21 = 0.17, k13 = 0.000015, k31 = 0.15)
ratios <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Cortex:plasma AUC, schematic reading",
               "Cortex:plasma AUC, printed equations",
               "Cortex:plasma AUC0-24, paper medians (565 / 28,314)",
               "Hippocampus:plasma AUC, schematic reading",
               "Hippocampus:plasma AUC0-24, paper medians (694.8 / 28,314)"),
  ratio = c(p[["k12"]] * p[["vc"]] / (p[["k21"]] * p[["vcx"]]),
            p[["vc"]] / p[["vcx"]],
            565 / 28314,
            p[["k13"]] * p[["vc"]] / (p[["k31"]] * p[["vhc"]]),
            694.8 / 28314)
)
knitr::kable(ratios, digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  abs(ratios$ratio[1] / ratios$ratio[3] - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(ratios$ratio[4] / ratios$ratio[5] - 1) < 0.30,
  ratios$ratio[2] > 20
)
```

# Simulation

No between-animal variances are reported, so every simulation below is a
typical-value simulation of a 282 g rat. The dose is given as a 2-min
intravenous infusion.

```{r simulate}
# The models carry no random effects, so every id is a typical animal; rxode2's
# note that a multi-subject solve has no omega is expected and is muffled alone.
solve_typical <- function(model, data, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxSolve(model, data, returnType = "data.frame", ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

mod <- readModelDb("Pais_2026_cefepime_rat")
wt <- 0.282

make_events <- function(arm, mg_per_kg, n_doses, t_end, id) {
  dose_times <- (seq_len(n_doses) - 1) * 24
  amt <- mg_per_kg * wt
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, t_end, by = 0.1), dose_times)))
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = dose_times, amt = amt, rate = amt / (2 / 60),
               evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs_times, amt = 0, rate = 0,
               evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(WT = wt, arm = arm) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}

events <- bind_rows(
  make_events("1,250 mg/kg daily x5", 1250, 5, 120, 1),
  make_events("1,593 mg/kg once", 1593, 1, 24, 2)
)
sim <- solve_typical(mod, events, keep = "arm")
sim_long <- sim |>
  select(id, arm, time, Plasma = Cc, Cortex = Cbrain_cortex,
         Hippocampus = Cbrain_hippocampus) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Plasma, Cortex, Hippocampus), names_to = "matrix",
               values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(matrix = factor(matrix, levels = c("Plasma", "Cortex", "Hippocampus")))
```

## Concentration-time profiles

Compare with the population (green) curves of Supplementary Figure S1: plasma
peaks of roughly 3,000-3,700 mg/L that decline to the low hundreds by 24 h,
and brain profiles that rise slowly to a peak of roughly 30-40 mg/L about 6-7 h
after each dose. The brain compartments equilibrate more slowly than plasma
declines, so their peak lags far behind the plasma peak.

```{r profiles, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(sim_long, aes(time, conc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Cefepime (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical-value cefepime profiles, 282 g rat with AKI",
       caption = "Compare with Pais 2026 Supplementary Figure S1 (population fits).") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# NCA over the first 24 h (PKNCA)

The paper's exposures are AUC0-24 and Cmax0-24 from the first dose.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_long |>
  filter(time <= 24, !is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(group = paste(arm, matrix, sep = " | "))
nca_dose <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1L, time == 0) |>
  select(id, arm, time, amt) |>
  inner_join(distinct(nca_conc, id, arm, group), by = c("id", "arm"),
             relationship = "one-to-many")

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | group + id, route = "intravascular",
                             duration = 2 / 60)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_wide |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm | matrix" = group, "Cmax0-24 (mg/L)" = cmax,
                "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 1, 1, 0))
```

## Comparison with the published exposures

The paper reports the median (IQR) over its 18 rats of each exposure, computed
from the individual empirical-Bayes profiles and pooled across both dosing arms
(Results, 'Cefepime pharmacokinetic model and estimated exposures'). The same
pooled median is used as the reference for each simulated arm.

```{r nca-compare}
paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~matrix,       ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "Plasma",       3480,    28314,
  "Cortex",       36.0,      565,
  "Hippocampus",  41.9,    694.8
)
reference <- tidyr::crossing(arm = unique(nca_conc$arm), paper) |>
  mutate(group = paste(arm, matrix, sep = " | ")) |>
  select(group, cmax, auclast)
simulated <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated, reference, by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value simulation vs the paper's median first-24-h exposures.")
```

`r attr(cmp, "footnote")`

The 1,593 mg/kg arm reproduces every pooled median to within 10%. The
1,250 mg/kg arm sits below them, and three of its rows are flagged: cortex
Cmax (-22%), cortex AUC0-24 (-23%) and plasma AUC0-24 (-29%). That is
expected for the lower dose against a median pooled across both doses, and the
hippocampus and plasma Cmax medians lie between the two arms. Every simulated
AUC0-24 and brain Cmax is inside the paper's IQR (for plasma AUC0-24,
9,737-41,639 mg*h/L); the two plasma Cmax values, 2,900 and 3,700 mg/L,
bracket its narrow IQR of 3,266-3,695 mg/L. The paper's values are medians of
individual empirical-Bayes exposures, and the between-rat spread is wide
(individual plasma AUC0-24 from about 7,000 to 52,000 mg*h/L in Figure 4a);
that variability is not reported as a variance and cannot be carried here, and
the split of the 18 rats between the two arms is not stated. Nothing has been
tuned.

```{r nca-assert}
sim_w <- nca_wide |> separate(group, c("arm", "matrix"), sep = " \\| ") |>
  left_join(paper, by = "matrix", suffix = c("_sim", "_paper"))
stopifnot(
  # Brain exposures within 25% of the pooled medians in both arms.
  all(abs(sim_w$auclast_sim / sim_w$auclast_paper - 1)[sim_w$matrix != "Plasma"] < 0.25),
  all(abs(sim_w$cmax_sim / sim_w$cmax_paper - 1) < 0.25),
  # Plasma AUC0-24 inside the published IQR.
  all(between(sim_w$auclast_sim[sim_w$matrix == "Plasma"], 9737, 41639))
)
```

# Exposure-seizure logistic models

Each logistic model gives `P(stage > 1) = expit(slope * (exposure - TC50))`.
The TC50s are printed; the slopes are not, and were digitised from the red
predicted-probability markers of Figure 5. Fitting `logit(p)` on exposure
freely, without holding TC50, returns TC50s within 1% of the printed ones
(30,370 vs 30,658.6; 766 vs 760.8; 44.9 vs 45.0; 842 vs 838.2; 48.1 vs 48.2),
which confirms the axis calibration.

```{r logistic-models}
lr_models <- tibble::tribble(
  ~model,                                             ~covariate,                         ~label,                         ~tc50,
  "Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_aucplasma_rat",       "AUC_CEFEPIME",                     "Plasma AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)",       30658.6,
  "Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_auccortex_rat",       "AUC_CEFEPIME_BRAIN_CORTEX",        "Cortex AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)",         760.8,
  "Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_cmaxcortex_rat",      "CMAX_CEFEPIME_BRAIN_CORTEX",       "Cortex Cmax0-24 (mg/L)",           45.0,
  "Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_auchippocampus_rat",  "AUC_CEFEPIME_BRAIN_HIPPOCAMPUS",   "Hippocampus AUC0-24 (mg*h/L)",    838.2,
  "Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_cmaxhippocampus_rat", "CMAX_CEFEPIME_BRAIN_HIPPOCAMPUS",  "Hippocampus Cmax0-24 (mg/L)",      48.2
)

solve_logistic <- function(model, covariate, x) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(x), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0)
  d[[covariate]] <- x
  out <- solve_typical(readModelDb(model), d)
  data.frame(exposure = x, prob = out$prob_racine_gt1)
}

curves <- lr_models |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(label = label, tc50 = tc50,
          solve_logistic(model, covariate, seq(0, 2.2 * tc50, length.out = 200)))
at_tc50 <- lr_models |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(label = label, solve_logistic(model, covariate, tc50))
knitr::kable(at_tc50, digits = 3, caption = "Each model returns 0.5 at its TC50.")
stopifnot(all(abs(at_tc50$prob - 0.5) < 1e-6))
```

```{r logistic-plot, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(curves, aes(exposure, prob)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = tc50), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Exposure", y = "P(seizure stage > 1)",
       caption = "Replicates the fitted probabilities of Pais 2026 Figure 5a, c-f; dashed = TC50.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Digitised points

The Figure 5a predicted probabilities that were read from the figure are
reproduced by the plasma model:

```{r digitised-check}
fig5a <- data.frame(
  exposure = c(20407, 23889, 32831, 35240, 35787, 36984, 41267, 43605, 46698),
  prob_figure = c(0.106, 0.193, 0.599, 0.716, 0.749, 0.775, 0.910, 0.933, 0.958)
)
chk <- solve_logistic("Pais_2026_cefepime_seizure_aucplasma_rat", "AUC_CEFEPIME",
                      fig5a$exposure) |>
  mutate(prob_figure = fig5a$prob_figure, diff = prob - prob_figure)
knitr::kable(chk, digits = 3)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$diff)) < 0.05)
```

## Linking the PK model to the seizure models

Feeding the typical-value first-24-h exposures from the PK model into the five
logistic models gives the seizure probability of a typical 282 g rat in each
arm. All five metrics agree that the typical rat sits below TC50, with the
higher single dose closer to it -- consistent with the paper's observation that
seizure-prone rats were those with the higher individual exposures.

```{r pk-to-pd}
typ_exposure <- nca_wide |>
  separate(group, c("arm", "matrix"), sep = " \\| ")
pk_pd <- bind_rows(
  typ_exposure |> filter(matrix == "Plasma") |>
    transmute(arm, model = lr_models$model[1], covariate = lr_models$covariate[1], x = auclast),
  typ_exposure |> filter(matrix == "Cortex") |>
    transmute(arm, model = lr_models$model[2], covariate = lr_models$covariate[2], x = auclast),
  typ_exposure |> filter(matrix == "Cortex") |>
    transmute(arm, model = lr_models$model[3], covariate = lr_models$covariate[3], x = cmax),
  typ_exposure |> filter(matrix == "Hippocampus") |>
    transmute(arm, model = lr_models$model[4], covariate = lr_models$covariate[4], x = auclast),
  typ_exposure |> filter(matrix == "Hippocampus") |>
    transmute(arm, model = lr_models$model[5], covariate = lr_models$covariate[5], x = cmax)
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(prob = solve_logistic(model, covariate, x)$prob) |>
  ungroup()
pk_pd |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Model" = model, "Exposure" = x,
                "P(stage > 1)" = prob) |>
  select(-covariate) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 1, 3))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Printed ODE typographical errors.** The cortex equation and the cortex
  output are printed with k12 in place of k21 and Acentral in place of Acortex.
  The model follows the Figure 3 schematic; the paper's own cortex and
  hippocampus exposures confirm that reading (see 'The printed equations').
* **Weight reference.** The covariate model is centred on "the median rat
  weight of the data set", which is not printed. The cohort mean, 282 g, is
  used (`WT / 0.282`, WT in kg). With a 17 g SD the choice moves kel and Vc by
  a few percent at most.
* **Weight exponents as printed.** Table 2 gives +0.75 on kel and +1 on Vc
  (Monolix `log(WT/WTref)` covariates, no RSE, so fixed). A positive exponent
  on a rate constant is unusual (allometry would give -0.25) but is carried as
  printed.
* **No between-animal variability.** Table 2 reports a 0.92 correlation between
  the kel and Vhippocampus random effects but no standard deviation for any
  random effect, so no eta is encoded and all simulations are typical-value.
* **No residual error.** Neither the error model nor its magnitude is reported;
  each output carries additive and proportional SDs fixed at 0.
* **Dosing duration.** The infusion length of the main study is not stated
  (the escalation study infused at 0.5-1 mL/min; the preliminary study over
  about 2 min). A 2-min infusion is used; it does not affect the brain
  exposures or AUC0-24.
* **Logistic slopes digitised.** The five logistic slopes are not printed and
  were digitised from Figure 5, holding the printed TC50s. Their placeholder
  additive residual (`fixed(0.001)`) is not from the source, whose likelihood is
  Bernoulli.
* **Hippocampus Cmax IQR.** The Results print the hippocampus Cmax0-24 IQR as
  31.7-62.8 mg/L and the Abstract as 13.7-62.8 mg/L; only the median (41.9) is
  used here.
* **Not encoded.** The Kaplan-Meier curve of time to seizure split at the
  plasma TC50 (Figure 5b) is a descriptive analysis with no fitted parameters.
